items.claim: The hoy onset at Isa.29.1 and the row's fold of the siege announcement into the sudden-reversal deliverance through Isa.29.8 rest on a continuous speaking voice with no addressee shift or fresh frame marker between them.
items.evidence: The row opens on the verse-initial woe onset ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל at oshb:Isa.29.1, after the setumah disclosed at web:Isa.28.29 (tier-3, single-witness); the reversal at Isa.29.5 turns on an adversative without a new vocative, massa, or speech-frame marker; the row closes on the setumah disclosed at web:Isa.29.8, immediately before the fresh imperative onset the next row correctly treats as its own seam at Isa.29.9.

items.claim: The strongest_rejected_alternative names isolating the sealed-book simile rather than the more obviously live rival of a fresh unit opening at Isa.29.13's own explicit speech-frame, which the row's own rationale must already argue against.
items.evidence: Isa.29.13 opens with a named divine-speech frame, וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲדֹנָ֗י (byte tier), introducing first-person indictment content in a form distinct from the third-person description running through Isa.29.9-Isa.29.12; the row's rationale defends keeping this frame inside the row ("continues the same indictment of lip-service worship rather than opening a fresh unit, since the addressee stays constant") without naming that seam as the disclosed rival. The alternative it names instead — isolating the sealed-book simile — is the weaker candidate: the setumah inside that simile (tier-3, single-witness) falls at Isa.29.12, mid-simile rather than at a unit edge, and the layer is explicitly never a boundary driver.

items.claim: The woe onset at Isa.29.15 and the row's fold of the potter/clay rebuke into the little-while reversal through Isa.29.21 rest on a shared-verb bridge that is honestly tiered at the consonantal-skeleton level rather than overclaimed as byte-identical.
items.evidence: The row opens on ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר at oshb:Isa.29.15, a verse-initial woe onset. The shared root recurs as הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב at oshb:Isa.29.16 and as יֵחָשֵֽׁב at oshb:Isa.29.17; the cantillation differs between the two sites (an atnach-class mark inside Isa.29.16 versus the verse-final mark at Isa.29.17), and the row discloses this difference rather than claiming a byte match, satisfying the honest-tier bar. Its front and close setumah disclosures at web:Isa.29.14 and web:Isa.29.21 match the inventory.
tier_citations: skeleton: oshb:Isa.29.16 / oshb:Isa.29.17 (shared root, differing accents)

items.claim: The koh-amar formula opening Isa.29.22 is correctly identified as a divine-speech frame with an explicit new addressee, a clean tier-1 warrant for closing off the preceding woe complex.
items.evidence: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית... at oshb:Isa.29.22 names Yahweh as speaker addressing the house of Jacob, matching the divine-frame class rather than the royal-messenger class attested only in the narrative zone; the front-seam setumah at web:Isa.29.21 is disclosed, and the interior of the three-verse row carries no further marked division.

items.claim: The hoy-plus-neum stack opening Isa.30.1 is a strong tier-1 warrant, and the row's closing quote is accurately sliced to fall after the verse's ketiv/qere pair rather than across it.
items.evidence: ה֣וֹי בָּנִ֤ים סֽוֹרְרִים֙ נְאֻם... at oshb:Isa.30.1 stacks a verse-initial woe onset with a postpositive divine-signature formula. The row's closing quote “a shame, and also a reproach” is drawn from the clause following the verse's ketiv/qere pair: the unpointed and pointed forms beginning כֹּ֣ל הבאיש... sit near the verse's opening, well before the quoted closing clause, so the slicing claim is accurate rather than merely asserted.

items.claim: The row correctly cuts on the massa header's own formal, verse-initial signal at Isa.30.6 even though it sits inside the surrounding woe-series zone, and discloses the thematic-continuity rival rather than suppressing it.
items.evidence: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּהֲמ֣וֹת נֶ֑גֶב... at oshb:Isa.30.6 matches the verse-initial massa-header class rather than the mid-verse header-reference or burden-noun classes. The row's own notes name the header-inside-woe-zone tension explicitly instead of silently overriding it, and the strongest_rejected_alternative names the live catchword-continuity rival on its actual textual grounds (shared Egypt-reliance subject, no addressee shift) rather than a strawman.

items.claim: The row folds the koh-amar citations at Isa.30.12 and Isa.30.15 into the tablet-commission unit's supporting texture without stating in words which speech-frame class they carry, leaving the frame identification implicit in the adjacent Holy One of Israel title rather than named.
items.evidence: Both quoted sites carry the Holy One of Israel title alongside the koh-amar formula, which correctly marks them as the divine-frame class rather than the royal-messenger class attested only in the narrative zone, but the boundary_rationale states only that they “elaborate the same commissioned address” and never names the frame as divine. The row's own opening seam at Isa.30.8 is otherwise cleanly argued from its second-person commission onset.
tier_citations: content: web:Isa.30.12 / web:Isa.30.15 (Holy One of Israel title, frame class unnamed)

items.claim: The reversal opening Isa.30.18 turns on the same therefore-connective used earlier in the chapter for judgment, now redirected toward mercy under the same divine voice — a genuine tonal turn rather than a fresh vocative — and no further tier-1 break interrupts the row through Isa.30.26.
items.evidence: וְלָכֵ֞ן יְחַכֶּ֤ה יְהוָה֙... at oshb:Isa.30.18 repeats the therefore-connective that earlier opened divine-frame indictment in this same chapter, here pivoted to grace. The row's front and close setumah disclosures at web:Isa.30.18 and web:Isa.30.26 match the inventory, and no hoy, massa, or koh-amar onset falls between them.
